entry.title: 1154 Pastaria
entry.content:
Gnocchi with a creamy mushroom sauce and spinach
Spinach and ricotta ravioli with a brown butter sauce
Garlic and rosemary roll

It confuses and perplexes us that we don’t see more pasta out there. Everyone loves pasta, it’s easy (relatively) to make, and it’s generally affordable. Maybe this is why 1154 is pumping every single time we walk past. But caution to those who don’t like communal dining experiences, this is a big-table-sit-with-other-people type of situation. This also means there’s no bookings, you just walk in, which suits us to the ground, but perhaps isn’t your cup of tea.

You could tell the pasta was homemade, and we have to give props to the gnocchi. The Fee-Rex isn’t a big gnocchi head, probably because so many of them are terrible, but these were little pillows of heaven. The sauce was also fantastic, the nuts added a great crunch and the mushroom bits were just the right size. Business Andy found the dish a little wearing over time, but perhaps that was because it started from such a lofty height.

The ravioli was also good. Both the raviolis themselves and the whole dish were generously sized. A little gripe about the bread. It was great for dipping into your pasta sauce, and it was affordable too. But it is not to be eaten alone, and if you don’t have bread then you will find yourself with too much leftover sauce. We recommend purchasing one bread each and dipping, but don’t bother eating it by itself.

entry.title: Nada Bakery
entry.content:
Steak, confit garlic, and parmesan pie
Pumpkin and bacon quiche
Apple danish
Carrot cake

Nada Bakery is a pretty popular place, especially for a rainy Sunday lunchtime. They were doing a steady trade in both dine-in and takeaway. We can see why. The cabinet had plenty of options and almost everything looked good. Their walls were covered in pie-related accolades, and having sampled their wares these seem deserved. The pie was quite special, although the pastry top was slightly over done.

The quiche was nothing special. This happens sometimes with quiches, where all you can taste is a little bit of bacon, while the pumpkin is visible but not tasteable. Is it that they haven’t roasted the pumpkin? Perhaps it just needed the addition of something else to help the pumpkin sing? A relish certainly wouldn’t have gone astray.

Danishes are one of God’s special tasty treats, and this one didn’t disappoint. Unconventionally they also offered a pineapple Danish, which we don’t think we’ve ever seen before. The carrot cake was trying hard, and they’d made real effort to jam pack it with nuts and fruit. They’d even gone to the effort to split it in 3 and ice between the layers. Unfortunately, this was their downfall. The icing was incredibly sweet, sickly even. We had assumed it was a cream cheese icing based on the look, but to taste there was little, or perhaps no cream cheese actually present. Unfortunately all the sugar ruined the whole thing and left you with that cloying quality on the back of your palate where you were just searching for water.

Speaking of, we saw that one other dine-in table had a bottle of water, but heaven knows where they got that. The ambiance wasn’t great - this place is definitely more of a bakery than a cafe. And half of the Fee-Rex’s chair was covered in dirt like it had been stacked up outside. But despite a few issues, we’d be very happy to try more of what Nada Bakery has to offer.

entry.title: The Bridge Bar & Restaurant
entry.content:
Cauliflower steak with mash and salad
Korean fried chicken with rice and slaw

On a Friday night at 6:30, The Bridge was doing a steady trade in the 50+ crowd. Perhaps it was the tellies showing 4 different sports simultaneously, perhaps it was the 70s jams with music videos played two seconds out of sync, perhaps it was the tantalising offer of free snacks at 7pm. We were very keen to ensure that we got our share of all - women’s motor racing, the Blues Brothers, and we made damn sure we had purchased a drink between 630 and 7 which gave us the coveted access to grab some fried goodies from the roving grazing platter which went past our table between 7 and 7:05.

Much as we love free fried goods, we paid a hefty price. Perhaps not financially, the monetary cost was actually quite reasonable, but the spiritual cost was heavy. We had three different cocktails and they were all bad. We do give The Bridge a modicum of credit for having a cocktail menu at all, as it was stretching their bounds. But the Tom Collins and Negroni were both awful, and the on-tap espresso martini wasn’t worth having.

Neither was the food. The cauliflower steak was woody as heck and not crispy as advertised. It at least had an interesting spice blend, which is more than you could say about the bland mash. The Korean fried chicken, despite a tasty sauce, was extremely dry. The rice was offensive. It had clearly been sitting in the rice cooker for some time, long enough to form a skin/shell. Give your rice a fluff, you monsters!

entry.title: Penthouse Cinema and Cafe
entry.content:
Mince & cheese pie
Fish & chips
Caramel slice

On a wintery Sunday at lunchtime, Penthouse Cinema & Cafe was absolutely heaving. The cinema tickets and cafe queue is shared and the line was almost out the door. Thanks to the recent release of Toy Story 5 and the latest Minions movie, there were kids everywhere, plus tonnes of senior citizens. The staff were rushed off their feet, but were still friendly and were clearly trying their best amidst difficult circumstances.

Given how busy it was, we thought we might be in for a treat. When the pie was $10, we accepted the price as an indicator of quality. How wrong we were. The pie did appear to be homemade and had good pastry, but what was up with that mince? You remember when you were flatting and you made that stir fry and it was just mince, onion and mixed veg, everybody hated it and you’d made a metric tonne of it? These pie innards were that, but without the veg. Where was the gravy? Where was the cheese? The salt? The pepper? And where was the heat? This thing was tepid at best. When we realised we’d paid $10 for it, we couldn’t help but laugh. And this was not an isolated incident - the man at the table next to us very angrily took his pie up to be reheated, then later, when his reheated pie finally showed up he got up again and told them that he just wanted a refund. This issue is systemic, people.

The fish and chips were better, but it’s hard to be worse. When the fish showed up looking very angular we were worried it was going to be a gross composite hoki fillet. To their credit, it was real fish fillet. To their debit, what was with the crumb? It was so crisp, when you tried to cut into it the shell immediately shattered and completely parted ways with the fish, which also disintegrated. This left you desperately picking little bits up from among the chips, we felt like anteaters trying to get little ants from a rotten log. The salad wasn’t great, why was there cabbage in it? We did at least enjoy the shoestring fries, and both the fries and the fish were hot out of the deep fryer.

The best part was the caramel slice. The portion was generous, the caramel thick, and the edge was extra sticky and delicious, a boon considering often the edge of a slice is often the worst bit.

Bringing us back down to earth; the espresso martinis. Firstly, they didn’t arrive until we were eating our food, which was already a long wait. They had a bitterness which was unpleasant - was the coffee burnt? Perhaps it was the ratios, something to do with the kahlua? Either way, they were bad. They weren’t quite Tirohana Estate bad, but still pretty bad.

entry.title: The Beijing Restaurant
entry.content:
Orange beef fried rice
Fried chicken
Fried dumplings

After something off a revamp, there’s some new additions to the menu at the Beijing, some new furniture, and a bit of a new vibe. We are long time Beijing patrons, with it being in our takeaway rotation. It made us nervous when we saw the revamp, which included the edition of a bunch of non-Chinese fried options (fried chicken and fish and chip shop options like nuggets and sausages). Is the Beijing struggling? We suggest the new menu, and the fact that they are generally not very busy when we get our takeaway, implies that they are.

We’re not helping much by not giving them a glowing review, but we can only review what arrived in front of us, and what arrived in front of us had some issues. The dumplings were super oily, were strangely floppy, and didn’t taste particularly good. The fried rice was only average, and the orange beef, while tasty and fresh, was perplexingly piled to one side instead of worked through it. It was like two separate meals and the stressful task of mixing ratios fell to us, the unsuspecting diners. And the fried chicken was just not quite good enough either, its extremities were borderline burnt, and there wasn’t nearly enough of the admittedly nice sweet soy sauce.

entry.title: Masala Cafe & Bar
entry.content:
Wellington lamb curry
Kadai paneer
Masala special naan
Plain naan

Indian restaurants, real talk. Get somebody to proofread your menus. Even a Microsoft Word spellcheck would have done you a lot of favours here. Although perhaps this is not a negative factor, but rather a marker of authenticity. Speaking of authentic, many restaurants claim to have homemade paneer, but you actually do. Kudos. Likewise the lamb in the mysterious “Wellington” curry was of good quality. The curry sauces themselves were perfectly good, but not exceptional.

What was exceptional was the masala special naan. This is a naan stuffed with chicken and vegetables, cut up like a pizza then served with butter chicken sauce for dipping. And it was killer, easily the best thing of the night. The plain naans definitely couldn’t keep pace, as they were a bit thin and dry.

entry.title: Viva Mexico
entry.content:
Enchiladas de birria
Feta and spinach quesadilla

We weren’t upset to be visiting Viva Mexico, they are already in our regular takeaway rotation, and they didn’t disappoint. Plus the feijoa margarita, an off menu suggestion from the waiter, was a triumph.

The food was all lovely and fresh, piping hot, and not too large for lunch. We even enjoyed the coleslaw that came with the enchiladas. Keep up the good work Viva Mexico.

entry.title: Nam Nam Bowen
entry.content:
Tofu bahn mi
Chicken fried rice

Nam nam caters to the business crowd, tired workers who just want to nip out for a bite as close to the office as possible. To that end the service and food delivery were fast, and the effort put into the dishes was acceptable but not more. Both meals were fine, you weren’t angry to eat them, but they hadn’t tried to climb the highest mountain.

The chicken had some pleasant crispness in spots but was pedestrian in flavour and the veg was just frozen veggie mix like your mum would put in a stir fry when she couldn’t be bothered. The banh MI had nice bread and fresh veg but the tofu lacked flavour. And don’t blame that on us ordering tofu, which can be very flavourful when done correctly.

entry.title: Newtown Seafood
entry.content:
Two chicken burgers
Battered fish Battered pineapple ring

The following is a true story. Two days ago , waiting for a bus, we were discussing dine in fish and chips shops and why they weren’t a thing. Today, the first place we saw to eat in Newtown was a dine in fish and chip shop that had just opened. Did we manifest this I to existence,? We see no other plausible explanation.

And thank god that we did, because it was really good. The fish was fresh, the batter, light, it came with a slice of lemon, and had just the right amount of salt on it. Likewise the chicken in the chicken burgers was crispy and delicious, perfectly fried, in fact the entire burger package was just right, fresh lettuce, not too much onion, soft buns. And it was real fried chicken,not a composite chicken smush patty like you might expect. And then the pineapple ring, it was absolutely covered in cinnamon and sugar, had a thick crispy batter, and was miraculously not too hot. We wondered, given how new this place is, whether what we were experiencing was the miraculous benefits of new fryer oil? I guess time will tell whether their quality remains high.

Given this glowing praise, we had to ask ourselves whether this was a 4. We decided it wasn’t, for the following reasons, but they weren’t far off. While the sign said “dine in” they hadn’t really gone to much effort to make that a good experience, it was chilly, there was no cutlery, few serviettes, really the only thing they did was put food on a tray instead of wrapping it up in paper. It really wouldn’t have taken much to make dining in a more pleasant experience. The chicken burger had nailed everything it set out to do, but it was conservative in its ambitions. An interesting sauce, a sneaky hash brown slipped in, or some pickle could all have bumped him closer to the top.

entry.title: PhuThai Esarn Restaurant
entry.content:
Khao soi chicken
Tofu pad Thai

When Business Andy came here for a work do a couple of years ago, he wasn’t that impressed. He had a great time, but he also drank far too much soju - perhaps this was a contributing factor. At any rate, two years later PhuThai Esarn Restaurant is still here, and continues to meh.

The Fee-Rex is a sucker for a pad Thai, even though many of them are only so-so, as was the case here. Also massive points off for some of your tofu being cold, a most unwelcome surprise. The khao soi just didn’t have an awful lot going on. There was some chilli oil on the side you could add to spice things up, but this was just bringing heat without doing anything for flavour. While the chicken was of acceptable quality, some crispening would have gone a long way to improving this dish.

We also boldly ordered two cocktails. We don’t normally bother with cocktails when a place only lists a handful of bog standards (pina colada, dark & stormy etc). However, PhuThai had a couple which sounded interesting - one made with Thai milk tea and another a play on a Mai Tai. These were disappointingly poor, and despite their simplicty took forever to make, arriving after our food. Also they contained short straws only 2.5mm longer than the drink, and shorter than the glass once they fell into the stupid divot in the centre. This meant at best you had to fish in with your fingers to get it, at worst it was fully submerged in the Mariana Trench.
